full_description: SDE-3 - Platform Backend Engineering | Distributed Systems | System Design About Mstack Mstack is building the world’s first AI-native chemical company. We combine AI, scientific R&D, software and real-world manufacturing to dramatically shorten the time it takes to move from a chemical idea to commercial production. Our technology powers Chemstack AI, our chemistry intelligence platform, as well as a growing set of products across commerce, internal operations, automation, analytics and decision-making. As Mstack grows, software is becoming the operating layer connecting our customers, scientists, commercial teams, supply chain and manufacturing ecosystem. About the Platform Team The Platform team builds the technology foundation that powers products across Mstack. Some of our systems support Chemstack AI, including agentic workflows, enterprise applications and scientific tooling. But the Platform team works across a much broader problem space. We are building systems for commerce, operational workflows, internal automation, metrics and decision-making, and shared capabilities that allow teams across Mstack to build products faster. Our goal is not to create isolated applications. We want to build reusable engineering primitives, services and platforms that can support multiple products while remaining reliable, secure and easy to evolve. The Role We are looking for an SDE-3 who is strong in backend engineering and enjoys solving difficult systems problems. You will design and build services that sit underneath critical products and workflows across Mstack. The problems you work on may involve distributed systems, asynchronous workflows, high-volume APIs, event-driven architectures, long-running jobs, data consistency, reliability and failure recovery. You will be expected to do more than implement a design handed to you. You should be able to take an ambiguous problem, understand the product and system constraints, design the architecture, reason through trade-offs, and take the system all the way to production. Systems design is core to this role. You should be comfortable thinking about what happens when traffic grows 10x, when dependencies fail, when a job runs for hours, when the same message is delivered twice, or when a system has to evolve without breaking existing users. What You'll Do Design backend systems Design services, APIs, data models and system boundaries for new products and platform capabilities. Work through trade-offs around consistency, availability, latency, throughput, maintainability and cost. Move comfortably from a product requirement to a concrete architecture and execution plan. Build distributed and asynchronous systems Design and operate systems involving queues, event streams, background jobs and workflow orchestration. Build systems where work may take seconds, minutes or hours and still needs to remain reliable across retries, crashes and deployments. Think carefully about idempotency, retries, ordering, concurrency, backpressure and failure recovery. Own systems end to end Take ownership from design through implementation, testing, deployment and production operations. Be responsible not only for whether the code works, but whether the system behaves correctly in production. Build APIs and platform services Design clean interfaces that allow other teams and products to build on top of your systems. Create reusable platform capabilities rather than repeatedly solving the same problem inside individual applications. Work with complex data flows Build systems that move and transform data across multiple services and workflows. Reason about transaction boundaries, consistency models, caching, indexing, schema evolution and data lifecycle. Engineer for reliability Design for failures before they happen. Build appropriate observability, metrics, logging and tracing so systems are understandable when something goes wrong. Participate in debugging production incidents and improve systems based on what we learn. Make systems scalable Identify bottlenecks before they become production problems. Improve application, database and infrastructure performance as workloads grow. Know when horizontal scaling solves the problem and when the architecture itself needs to change. Raise engineering standards Contribute to architecture reviews, code reviews and engineering discussions. Help improve how the team approaches system design, testing, reliability and maintainability. Mentor engineers when appropriate and help the team make better technical decisions. What We're Looking For 7+ years of professional software engineering experience, primarily working on backend or distributed systems. Strong fundamentals in data structures, algorithms, operating systems, networking and databases. Strong experience designing and operating production backend systems. Strong system-design ability and clear reasoning about architectural trade-offs. Experience designing APIs, service boundaries and data models. Experience with relational databases, including indexing, transactions, locking and query performance. Experience with asynchronous processing using queues, event systems or background workers. Strong understanding of concurrency, retries, idempotency and common distributed-system failure modes. Experience debugging production systems using logs, metrics and traces. Understanding of caching and the consistency trade-offs it introduces. Experience building systems that have scaled meaningfully in traffic, data volume or complexity. Strong coding ability in at least one backend language such as Python, Go, Java or similar. Experience with at least one major cloud platform such as AWS, GCP or Azure. Ability to independently take a technical problem from ambiguity to production. Systems Design Expectations Systems design is a significant part of the engineering bar for this role. We care less about memorised templates and more about whether you can identify the important constraints, make assumptions explicit, and reason through trade-offs. You should be comfortable discussing questions such as: How would you design a service that needs to handle millions of requests reliably? When would you choose synchronous communication versus an event-driven architecture? How do you make a job safe to retry? How do you prevent duplicate processing in a distributed system? When should data live in one database versus separate services? How do you evolve an API without breaking existing consumers? How do you design for partial failure and slow dependencies? How would you build a workflow that needs to run reliably for several hours? When should you use caching, and how do you keep cached data correct? How do you identify whether a scaling problem comes from compute, database, network or architecture? Nice to Have Go or Python in production. PostgreSQL or other relational databases at scale. Kafka, SQS, Pub/Sub or similar messaging systems. Kubernetes and containerized production environments. Infrastructure as code and strong production operations practices. Workflow orchestration systems. Microservices or service-oriented architectures. Distributed tracing and observability platforms. Multi-tenant B2B systems and enterprise security patterns. High-volume commerce or transaction systems. AI or agentic systems, including MCP or tool-based agent architectures. Search, indexing, retrieval infrastructure, or data-intensive analytics platforms. How We Think About Backend Engineering We care about engineers who understand that production systems are more than application code. A strong backend engineer should be able to ask: Where can this system fail? What happens when the database becomes slow? Can this request safely be retried? What if the same event arrives twice? What state should be persisted? Which operations require strong consistency? What should happen during a partial outage? How will we understand this system six months after it goes live? What assumptions stop being true when the workload grows 10x? Are we building something reusable or adding another one-off service? Writing clean code matters. Knowing what system should be built in the first place matters even more at this level. Why Mstack Work on systems that connect software and the physical world The systems we build influence real scientific, commercial and operational workflows rather than existing only behind a screen. Solve problems across multiple domains You may work on AI infrastructure one quarter and commerce or operational systems the next. The engineering principles remain the same, but the problems are rarely repetitive. Build foundations, not just features The Platform team is responsible for capabilities that multiple products and teams can build upon. Good technical decisions have leverage across the company. Own meaningful architecture Many of the systems that Mstack will need at scale are being designed today. You will have the opportunity to shape those systems rather than simply operate infrastructure designed years ago. Work close to the problem Engineers work directly with product teams and domain experts. You will understand why a system is being built, not just receive a ticket describing what to implement. What Success Looks Like Within your first few months, you should be able to independently own a meaningful backend system or platform capability from design to production. You should be able to understand an ambiguous problem, propose an architecture, identify its risks and trade-offs, and drive the implementation. Over time, we expect you to become one of the engineers people rely on for difficult systems-design decisions. You should raise the quality of the systems around you through better architecture, stronger reliability practices, thoughtful abstractions and high engineering standards. We value demonstrated engineering ability over a particular degree or career path. If you have built systems you are proud of, we would love to hear about what you designed, what scale it operated at, where it failed, and what you would do differently today.

Create Quality Intelligence using NLP, clustering, causal analysis, and machine learning to classify non-conformances, identify recurring root causes, predict recurrence, score effectiveness, and predict closure delays — aligned with Mondelēz CAPA and Quality Policy (QP) frameworks. Develop calibration and measurement-system analytics for calibration overdue risk, instrument drift, measurement uncertainty, compliance gaps, and quality impact from calibration failures. Use NLP and GenAI to extract insights from QCMS audit reports, CAPA narratives, consumer complaints, deviations, SOPs, HACCP/Food Safety Plans (FSP), maintenance logs, and supplier communications; enable AI-assisted quality investigations and audit preparation. Build analytics connecting supplier quality, incoming-material risk, and customer-quality outcomes to create end-to-end quality visibility across the supply chain — from raw material to consumer. Build quality dashboards, risk scorecards, alerts, and self-service analytics for Q&FS, BU Quality, Global Food Safety, Plant Operations, and RDQ stakeholders. Manufacturing Data Science — Core / Supporting Focus Build IIoT-enabled analytics using data from PLCs, SCADA, historians, MES , sensors, edge devices, vision systems, LIMS, and QMS platforms. Develop predictive-maintenance models for equipment failure, asset health, remaining useful life, condition-based monitoring, anomaly detection, and maintenance prioritisation — leveraging IL6S (Integrated Lean Six Sigma) loss-elimination methodology. Support automated process control and closed-loop control through process modelling, deviation prediction, setpoint recommendations, and feedback-driven control strategies. full_description: About Us Meesho - Every story here begins with a spark of ambition and a touch of entrepreneurial magic. We're not just a platform — we're your partner in transforming dreams into reality. Our Mission Democratising internet commerce for everyone - Meesho started with a single idea in mind: to be an e-commerce destination for the next billion Indian consumers and enable small businesses to succeed online. We provide sellers with a range of industry-first benefits such as zero commission and affordable shipping costs, growing their business by tapping the company's massive customer base, state-of-the-art tech infrastructure, and pan-India logistics at cost through third-party logistics providers and our in-house logistics arm Valmo, in an 'Everyday Low Cost' channel for sellers. Affordable, relatable merchandise mirroring local markets has helped us make inroads with first-time internet users in the country. We cater to an underserved and unique customer base and cover every serviceable pincode in the country. Our unique business model and continuous innovation have enabled us to become the first Indian horizontal e-commerce company. Know more about Meesho here: https://www.meesho.io/ About Valmo And The Data Science Team Valmo is Meesho's own logistics arm, built to give sellers and customers cutting-edge, low-cost logistics and supply chain support. Supply Chain Network Optimization sits at the heart of the Valmo Data Science team: we design and plan the network that moves Valmo's shipments every day, from first-mile pickup through sort centres and line haul to last-mile delivery. We use OR, MILP, stochastic optimisation, simulation, ML and DL across network design, first/middle/last-mile optimisation, capacity planning and delivery promise, and we build for the long term, not just today's problems. This role is for someone ready to execute at speed, with a growth mindset, to build and scale these models. About The Role As a Data Scientist 3(Operations Research), you will own a workstream within Valmo network design — not just a model. You will be accountable for the North Star Metric of that workstream (cost per shipment, end-to-end shipment speed, network capacity utilisation, on-time delivery, delivery promise), set its OR/ML roadmap, and mentor DS1s and DS2s in delivering it. You will take ambiguous, loosely-defined business problems, decide which ones are worth solving, formulate them mathematically, and ship optimization systems that run Valmo's network every day. Workstreams span network design, routing and scheduling across the first, middle and last mile. What You Will Do Own a workstream end to end: decide which problems are worth solving, set and drive its roadmap, and be accountable for the movement of its metrics. Formulate complex, loosely defined business problems in network design, routing, scheduling, allocation and capacity planning as LP, MILP, MINLP or constraint programming models, with explicit assumptions. Solve them at scale with decomposition (Benders, Lagrangian relaxation, column generation, branch-and-price), heuristics and metaheuristics (large neighbourhood search, ALNS, tabu search) and constraint programming, within real planning-time budgets. Handle uncertainty with stochastic, robust and chance-constrained optimisation, and test decisions through simulation before they reach the ground. Combine OR with ML and DL, such as demand and volume forecasting, ETA prediction and learned heuristics, wherever it improves the decision. Write production-grade code and work with engineering to ship solvers and models into systems that run every day, with testing, monitoring and reproducible pipelines. Use AI coding agents as part of how you build, and verify the formulations, code and results they produce. Mentor DS1s and DS2s on formulation, modelling craft and code quality; align the roadmap with product, engineering, operations and business; and explain trade-offs to senior leaders in decision terms. Publish your work at A* conferences and journals, as part of a team with a highly innovative work culture. What You Will Need Bachelor's, Master's or PhD in Operations Research, Industrial Engineering, Applied Mathematics, Statistics, Computer Science or a related quantitative field. 5–8 years of experience (or 3+ years with a PhD) applying operations research to real-world problems, with optimisation models deployed in production. Deep expertise in mathematical optimisation (LP, MILP, network flows, integer and combinatorial optimisation), with a proven ability to formulate ambiguous problems, design heuristics, and break complex problems into simpler sub-problems. Experience with large-scale solution methods (decomposition, column generation, heuristics and metaheuristics, constraint programming) and with optimisation under uncertainty and simulation. Hands-on experience with solvers and modelling tools such as Gurobi, CPLEX, OR-Tools (including CP-SAT), HiGHS, Pyomo or PuLP. Strong programming: expert Python and SQL, PySpark or similar for large datasets, and solid software engineering (object-oriented design, Git, testing, code review). Fluency with AI coding agents, with the judgement to check their output. Working knowledge of ML and DL (forecasting, regression, tree-based models, neural networks) and of how to combine them with optimisation. It moves beyond demand intake and status coordination to owning product outcomes, roadmap decisions, prioritization, adoption and measurable business value. The TPM owns the Sales vertical product direction and business outcomes while partnering with platform Product Owners, Data Architects, Business Analysts, Scrum Masters, engineering, quality and compliance teams that retain accountability for their respective platform, architecture and delivery responsibilities. Key Responsibilities Product vision, strategy and roadmap Define and communicate a multi-quarter data-product vision and roadmap for Commercial Sales, aligned with Commercial Unit priorities and the broader Data & AI strategy. Translate business problems such as field effectiveness, targeting and customer engagement into validated product opportunities, data requirements and measurable outcomes. Prioritize the roadmap and backlog using business value, urgency, strategic alignment, effort, risk, compliance, capacity and dependency trade-offs; make and defend scope decisions with leadership. Align the Sales roadmap with reusable enterprise capabilities, platform roadmaps and relevant AI innovation initiatives before approving vertical-specific development. Validate problems and proposed product concepts through interviews, workflow observation, prototypes, data analysis, usability testing and field feedback. Own product priorities, backlog ordering and timely scope decisions; partner with the Business Analyst to translate outcomes into epics, features, user stories, data requirements and acceptance criteria. Partner with the Scrum Master so planning refinement, reviews and delivery ceremonies support product priorities and timely decisions. Work with data engineers, analysts, ML engineers, quality teams and architects to resolve product questions and make informed value, usability, risk and sequencing trade-offs. Establish business acceptance criteria, coordinate UAT with authorized Sales stakeholders and secure business sign-off before release. Ensure critical Sales measures are reconciled across source systems, data products and consuming reports before production adoption. Coordinate product acceptance and operational handover to downstream analytics and reporting teams, including documentation, access, support ownership and known limitations. Track delivery and product health, proactively surfacing risks, dependencies, quality concerns, cost considerations and mitigation decisions. Stakeholder, portfolio and operating-model leadership Act as the single point of accountability and voice of the product for Commercial business partners, Sales Operations, field leadership and technology stakeholders. Lead regular Sales product reviews covering roadmap, value realized, adoption, product health, dependencies, risks and decisions required. Lead quarterly demand, capacity and sequencing discussions for the Sales data-product portfolio, balancing business value, urgency, strategic alignment, risk, technical dependencies and available delivery capacity. Assess existing enterprise data products, approved patterns and reusable platform capabilities before starting new development. Contribute to maintaining the Sales DA&AI operating model, decision rights and RACI, recommending updates when product, platform or delivery accountabilities change. Provide concise executive updates and evidence-based investment recommendations, including the consequences of funding, capacity and sequencing decisions. Data, AI and regulated-environment stewardship Champion and apply architecture, data-governance, privacy, security, quality and compliance standards established by the accountable enterprise teams. Promote trusted business definitions, data quality, lineage, appropriate access and a consistent source of truth for Sales and Commercial measures. Identify and validate Sales problems that may benefit from analytics, machine learning, generative AI or agentic capabilities. Partner with Business Analysts and engineering teams to assess feasibility, data readiness, responsible-AI considerations and measurable business value. Support the transition of successful proofs of concept into governed, supportable and adoptable Sales products. Value realization, adoption and lifecycle management Define success measures before investment and track outcomes after release, using appropriate business, product, data-quality, adoption and delivery measures. Drive change management, training, communications and field enablement so intended users adopt and benefit from the products. Continuously improve products through evidence-based releases, address low adoption or quality concerns and retire low-value or duplicative capabilities. Role Accountability and Decision Rights The TPM is accountable for why the product is needed, whom it serves, what outcomes it must deliver, what is prioritized and whether value is realized. The TPM partners with the Business Analyst on detailed requirements, the Scrum Master on delivery ceremonies, the Data Architect on architecture and governance standards, engineering and quality teams on implementation and validation, and platform Product Owners on reusable capabilities and technical roadmaps. The quality dimension is your home base — QCMS performance, audit readiness, QFS intelligence, compliance risk — but you will also extend the Central Analytics team's manufacturing data-science portfolio by helping scale predictive maintenance, process optimisation, and IIoT-driven analytics across the plant network.
